children: Apple Inc. (AAPL, Financials) The tech giant is giving the top post to John Ternus at a time when expectations for the stock are already off the charts.

Tim Cook will step down as chief executive officer on Sept. 1 and become executive chairman after 15 years managing the company, with Ternus to succeed him. The timing makes this succession more relevant for investors.

Shares of Apple have risen about 40% in the past 12 months and recently closed at $319.70, giving the company a market capitalization of roughly $5 trillion. The stock trades at approximately 33 times forward earnings, too.

That provides little room for a weak product cycle or slower growth for Ternus. Ahead of the leadership transition, Bank of America analyst Wamsi Mohan maintained a Buy rating and a $380 price target.

Ternus is likely to have to make early judgments about investing on artificial intelligence, product strategy and hardware expansion. Apple is anticipated to announce a foldable iPhone during its first big public product event, scheduled for Sept. 9.

The bar is high, but so is the potential. Apple has already traded at a historic value high and investors will be looking to see if Ternus can justify that premium with faster AI execution, better product cycles and ongoing hardware demand.

title: Apple's New CEO Is Inheriting a Nearly $5 Trillion Problem
